title: The synergistic anti-inflammatory effect of pterostilbene and honokiol on LPS-stimulated PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophages.
authors: Zhu, Cuicui; Shen, Chenye; Wang, Jing; Yuan, Minjia; Di, Lei; Li, Qi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究紫檀芪和厚朴酚在巨噬细胞中的协同抗炎作用，仅涉及小分子-蛋白对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The cosmetics industry increasingly prioritizes the development of formulations that are both safe and effective. This study aimed to investigate the synergistic anti-inflammatory effects of pterostilbene (Pt) and honokiol (Ho) in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated THP-1 macrophages and to evaluate their systemic safety using the Threshold of Toxicological Concern (TTC) framework. METHODS: Human THP-1 monocytes were differentiated with PMA and stimulated with LPS to model inflammatory conditions. Pt and Ho were tested individually and in combination for their ability to suppress macrophage proliferation and proinflammatory cytokine production (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6). Synergistic effects were assessed through combination index and isobolographic analyses. NF-kappaB pathway modulation was evaluated via Western blot, and molecular docking was performed to explore compound-target interactions. Maximum systemically safe concentrations were calculated using TTC values integrated with default dermal absorption percentages and product-specific exposure parameters. RESULTS: Pt and Ho significantly inhibited LPS-induced macrophage proliferation and cytokine production, both individually and in combination. Combination index and isobologram analyses confirmed synergistic suppression of cytokines at low, non-cytotoxic concentrations. Both compounds attenuated NF-kappaB activation; however, no statistical synergy was observed at the signalling level, indicating coordinated but distinct mechanisms. Molecular docking revealed direct binding of Pt to NF-kappaB, while Ho exhibited no appreciable binding, further supporting mechanistic divergence. TTC-based calculations established systemically safe concentration limits for Pt and Ho across various cosmetic product categories. CONCLUSION: Pt and Ho exert synergistic anti-inflammatory effects in macrophages and can be safely used within systemically acceptable concentration limits in cosmetic formulations. These findings support their development as a multifunctional combination targeting inflammation-related skin conditions, while underscoring the need for further investigation into dermal safety, optimized dosing strategies and broader mechanistic pathways.
abstract_zh: 目的：化妆品行业日益重视开发既安全又有效的配方。本研究旨在探讨紫檀芪（pterostilbene, Pt）和厚朴酚（honokiol, Ho）在脂多糖（lipopolysaccharide, LPS）刺激的THP-1巨噬细胞中的协同抗炎作用，并利用毒理学关注阈值（Threshold of Toxicological Concern, TTC）框架评估其系统安全性。方法：人THP-1单核细胞经PMA分化并用LPS刺激以模拟炎症条件。单独及联合测试Pt和Ho抑制巨噬细胞增殖和促炎细胞因子产生（TNF-alpha、IL-1beta、IL-6）的能力。通过联合指数和等辐射分析评估协同效应。采用Western blot检测NF-kappaB通路调节，并进行分子对接以探索化合物-靶点相互作用。最大系统安全浓度通过TTC值结合默认皮肤吸收百分比和产品特定暴露参数计算得出。结果：Pt和Ho单独及联合使用均显著抑制LPS诱导的巨噬细胞增殖和细胞因子产生。联合指数和等辐射图分析确认在低、非细胞毒性浓度下对细胞因子具有协同抑制作用。两种化合物均减弱NF-kappaB激活；然而，在信号水平未观察到统计学协同效应，表明机制协调但不同。分子对接显示Pt直接结合NF-kappaB，而Ho无明显结合，进一步支持机制差异。基于TTC的计算确定了Pt和Ho在各种化妆品产品类别中的系统安全浓度限值。结论：Pt和Ho在巨噬细胞中发挥协同抗炎作用，并可在系统可接受浓度限值内安全用于化妆品配方。这些发现支持其作为针对炎症相关皮肤问题的多功能组合的开发，同时强调需进一步研究皮肤安全性、优化剂量策略及更广泛的机制通路。
